title: Add Digit Lists
statement:
Add two non-negative integers that are stored as linked lists of decimal digits, least significant digit first.

Contract
- Each node holds one digit 0-9. The head is the ones place, the next node is the tens place, and so on. So `2 -> 4 -> 3` represents 342.
- Return the head of a new list holding the sum in the same format. Do not reuse or modify nodes of the inputs.
- The result has as many nodes as the longer input, plus one extra node holding 1 when a carry is left over after the last digit. Do not strip leading zeros of the inputs (so `0 -> 0` plus `0` is `0 -> 0`).
- A null list counts as the number 0. If both are null the result is the single node `0`.
- The numbers can be far larger than any primitive type, so add digit by digit.

Examples
- `2 -> 4 -> 3` plus `5 -> 6 -> 4` returns `7 -> 0 -> 8` (342 + 465 = 807).
- `9 -> 9 -> 9 -> 9` plus `1` returns `0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 0 -> 1`.
- `0` plus `0` returns `0`.
hints: Add the way you do on paper: start at the ones place and carry into the next place. Both lists already start there.
Walk both lists together; a list that has run out contributes 0. Keep going while either list has nodes or a carry remains, so the last carry gets its own node.

Each step computes sum = a + b + carry, appends sum % 10, and carries sum / 10. A dummy head node avoids special-casing the first append. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the result, where n is the length of the longer list.
inputSyntax: Input: two digit lists separated by |, least significant digit first, for example: 2 4 3 | 5 6 4
